summary: Sega's motorcycle-racing series built around Yu Suzuki's Super Scaler arcade technology, ride-on cabinets, and later home/handheld conversions.

entries.title: Hang-On

emulation.notes: MAME preserves the arcade software; original ride-on hardware is required for full body-control fidelity.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Sega Super Scaler arcade presentation with modern scaling; physical ride-on controls only on original hardware

primary.version: Original Sega deluxe ride-on arcade release
primary.why: Hang-On was designed for Sega's Super Scaler arcade hardware and introduced a motion-controlled motorcycle cabinet where the player's body movement controlled the bike. The deluxe arcade cabinet is the highest-fidelity and most authentic version; home ports simplify the controls and presentation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME/original hardware; choose the deluxe ride-on cabinet where available for the intended full-body controls.

entries.remaster_caveats: SG-1000 Hang-On II is a simplified port, not a true sequel; Hang-On Jr. is an arcade release based on the Master System port.

entries.title: Super Hang-On
entries.definitive_edition: Limited Edition Hang-On arcade for main route; Genesis/Mega Drive and Nintendo 3DS for exclusive extras

emulation.emulator: MAME / Genesis Plus GX / Nintendo 3DS hardware
emulation.notes: Use arcade hardware or MAME for the primary, Genesis/Mega Drive for original mode, and 3DS hardware for stereoscopic presentation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Full motorcycle arcade cabinet for primary; stereoscopic 3D only on 3DS

primary.version: 1991 Limited Edition Hang-On full motorcycle cabinet
primary.why: Super Hang-On is the arcade sequel to Hang-On, with four continent-based courses and turbo speed. The 1991 Limited Edition Hang-On arcade release puts Super Hang-On into the full motorcycle cabinet style used by the original Hang-On, making it the best cabinet-fidelity route; the Genesis/Mega Drive version adds an original sponsor-and-upgrade mode, and the 3DS version adds stereoscopic 3D and tilt controls.
primary.how_to_play: Play Limited Edition Hang-On or the original arcade version in MAME/original hardware for the main route; sample Genesis/Mega Drive original mode and 3DS stereoscopic mode for their exclusive presentation/content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original mode with sponsors, earned money, bike component upgrades, and password-saved progression.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive original mode after the arcade route.
secondary.why: Arcade is the cabinet-fidelity route; Genesis/Mega Drive adds a distinct progression mode not present in the arcade.

secondary.exclusive_content: Stereoscopic 3D conversion with tilt controls emulating the arcade bike lean.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the 3DS release for the stereoscopic and tilt-control presentation.
secondary.why: It is lower cabinet fidelity than arcade hardware but has a unique 3D presentation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Wii Virtual Console billboard edits make it less pure than arcade preservation; Genesis compilations reissue the home port, not the arcade cabinet.

entries.title: Hang-On GP

emulation.notes: Use original Sega Saturn hardware or a compatible Saturn emulator.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Sega Saturn 3D presentation with modern scaling

primary.why: Hang-On GP is a polygon-based Hang-On series sequel developed by Genki and published by Sega only for Sega Saturn. With no other sourced release platform, the Saturn version is the complete primary route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Sega Saturn hardware or a compatible Saturn emulator.

entries.remaster_caveats: Known as Hang-On GP '95 in North America and Hang-On GP '96 in Europe; no sourced remaster or port.
